The honest range below leans to the LOW half of generic norms because Intima has no revenue, no traction, no entity and (as far as the record shows) no investor-grade founder pedigree signal.

comp_takeaways: Every named comp that raised ≥$1M had either a famous operator founder (Misters, Mosaic, Even), a clinic network or revenue (Allo, Bold Care, Proactive), or both. Intima currently has none of those signals.

Post-money valuations were NOT disclosed for any comp round we found. We therefore do not present a 'comp-implied valuation'; our ranges come from generic Indian angel norms (sourced blogs) discounted for Intima's stage. This is an estimate.
Funding ≠ success: Misters raised ₹3.5 cr in 2019 and reportedly shows only ≈₹33 lakh FY25 revenue (unverified). Investors will check traction, not the idea.
Closest practical analogue for a first cheque is the angel/pre-seed norm (₹20–50 L), not the $1–5M institutional rounds above.

verdict.text: Viable only as a lean, doctor-channel business. At the default sliders the model does NOT break even within 12 months and peaks at roughly ₹31 L of cumulative cash need (calculator output; ESTIMATE) — even a hopeful setting (1,000 users/month, 35% D30, 8% premium, 10% supplement attach, 15 paying clinics) still loses ≈₹7 K/month at month 12. So outside money is needed to survive the tour, and the business only works if retention, clinic fees and CAC beat the defaults. Supplements carry the margin; Premium is only meaningful with strong retention; hardware is a trust feature, not a profit centre. Move the sliders to see what each assumption must be for viability. All inputs are ESTIMATES.

compliance.detail: Health supplements/nutraceuticals need an FSSAI licence (central licence per the 2022 nutraceutical direction, per search summary), compliant labelling ('not for medicinal use'), and only structure/function claims — no 'treats ED / low testosterone / PCOS'. Using a licensed third-party manufacturer is cheapest but you remain responsible for claims.
compliance.action: Use a licensed manufacturer; get label/claim review before launch; no disease claims anywhere (app, doctor decks, ads).

compliance.area: BP monitor / thermometer / ring claims — CDSCO
compliance.detail: Under Medical Devices Rules 2017, digital thermometers are generally Class A and BP monitors Class B (licence from the State Licensing Authority) per search summary. Reselling third-party devices needs the maker/importer to hold valid registration/licence; Intima must not make diagnostic claims ('detects hypertension', 'predicts ovulation/fertility') from a ring or BBT sensor.
compliance.action: Resell only CDSCO-registered devices; keep copy to 'tracking / wellness'; legal review before any claim; confirm classification on the CDSCO site.

compliance.detail: DPDP Rules notified 13 Nov 2025; most substantive obligations apply after 18 months (≈13 May 2027) per search summary. Health data of adults and children needs notice, purpose-limited consent, breach handling, deletion, and verifiable parental consent for minors (narrow healthcare exemptions).
compliance.action: Build consent + notice + deletion/export flows before the clinic tour; log processors (cloud, AI provider); designate a grievance contact.

compliance.detail: Only Registered Medical Practitioners may consult and prescribe, within the guideline's drug lists (O/A/B/prohibited incl. Schedule X) and record-keeping rules; the platform must verify RMP registration and keep consent/records. The AI companion must not present itself as a doctor.
compliance.action: Contract RMPs, display registration numbers, store consult records, keep AI disclaimers on every screen.

compliance.detail: No commissions/fee-splitting to doctors for referrals (IMC 2002 clause 6.4 currently operative; NMC 2023 reg. 9 in abeyance — per search summary).
compliance.action: Design the channel as clinic SaaS + education, not per-referral payouts; lawyer sign-off.

compliance.detail: ASCI/consumer-law exposure for 'doctor-recommended', 'clinically proven', outcome claims. Do not use claims without evidence.
compliance.action: Evidence file for every claim; no outcome numbers until measured.

privacy_honesty.title: Privacy-claims honesty (must match the app and OPERATING.md)
true_statements: Health logs sync to the cloud — they are NOT only on the device.
AI chat messages are sent to a third-party AI provider.
Consult messages are encrypted at rest with an operator-held key — this is NOT end-to-end encryption; the operator can technically decrypt.
No-login access reduces account data collected, but is not the same as 'no data collected'.
never_say: '100% on-device', 'never leaves your phone', 'we cannot read your data', 'end-to-end encrypted', 'anonymous' (unless true and verified), 'HIPAA/GDPR certified'.
privacy_honesty.why_it_matters: Women's-health apps are distrusted on data (see social radar cluster 'c-privacy'); investors like Rainmatter weigh privacy ethos; DPDP and consumer law treat misleading privacy claims as risk. An honest, specific privacy page is a differentiator; an overclaim is a liability in due diligence.
